report:
### Research Conclusion

Contrary to your initial assumption, medical evidence indicates that regular intake of cranberry products **can** help reduce the risk of recurrent cystitis (urinary tract infections) in women.

### Scientific Evidence & Mechanism

* **Biological Mechanism:** Cranberries contain bioactive compounds called proanthocyanidins (PACs). PACs prevent uropathogenic *Escherichia coli* (the primary cause of UTIs) from adhering to the urothelial cells lining the bladder wall, hindering infection establishment.
* **Cochrane Systematic Review:** A 2023 update of the Cochrane systematic review evaluating randomized controlled trials concluded that cranberry products significantly reduce the risk of symptomatic, culture-verified UTIs in women with recurrent UTIs.
* **Clinical Guidelines:** Professional organizations, including the American Urological Association (AUA), provide a conditional recommendation (Grade C evidence) supporting cranberry prophylaxis as a non-antibiotic preventive option for women with recurrent UTIs.

While evidence does not support efficacy across all patient populations (such as elderly individuals or patients with bladder-emptying disorders), it strongly supports cranberry intake for women susceptible to recurrent cystitis.

### Sources Relied On

* Cochrane Review Evidence Summary: https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001321_cranberries-preventing-urinary-tract-infections
* PubMed (Cochrane Review Abstract): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37068952/
* Clinical Guideline Summary: https://www.droracle.ai/articles/599751/is-cranberry-extract-effective-in-preventing-recurrent-urinary-tract
